output.title: Designing for seasonality starts with one workflow
output.body:
This is for the owner of a 1–10 person business who has tried ChatGPT but has not wired AI into a real workflow yet.

Seasonality stops being abstract when you pin it to one recurring task. For many small businesses, that is customer replies, fulfilment updates, invoicing, or lead follow-up. The useful question is not “Can AI help?” It is “Which repeatable task turns into the bottleneck first?”

Start there and look at the decision you already face: are you delaying replies, considering temporary help, or just absorbing the extra work? Write down what that slowdown costs you in time and where it shows up in customer responsiveness. Then define success in plain language: faster replies, less backlog, or fewer hours spent on the same admin. No theatre needed.

Next, test the shape of the task. Can it be split into a repeatable, rule-based part and a judgment part? Answering FAQs, generating invoices, or qualifying leads often can. High-stakes decisions, custom exceptions, and anything that needs careful human approval stay with you. That line matters.

Then check where the work already lives. If it sits in email, a CRM, a spreadsheet, or another SaaS tool you already use, it is a cleaner candidate for a bounded automation pilot. If it does not repeat cleanly, or it depends on sensitive judgment, continue manually or hire. Both are valid answers.

A practical next step: spend about 10 minutes documenting one peak-season task, including inputs, rules, output, and how often it repeats. That gives you a better build-versus-hire decision before you think about tools.
